correctness.rationale: For X=A^(1/2) B^(1/2) A^(-1/2), the near-geometric endpoint is XX*, X^2 is similar to B, and the trace difference is half the squared Frobenius norm of X-X*. When A=aP+b(I-P), this is (a-b)^2/(ab) times the squared Frobenius norm of P B^(1/2)(I-P). The Hermitian difference S-JSJ, J=2P-I, has positive eigenvalues twice the off-diagonal singular values; Ky Fan weak majorization bounds their squared sum by the extreme-paired spectral spread. Independent balanced two-dimensional blocks attain this bound, the diagonal arrangement yields zero, and connectedness fills the interval. Cayley-Hamilton gives the two-by-two commutator identity and determinant preservation gives its eigenvalue formula. The full symbolic proof was reconstructed with normalization and all multiplicity/rank limits; 2,950 exact rational checks corroborate without replacing the infinite family proof.

The exact commutator energy makes the trace dilation sensitive to noncommutativity in every finite dimension; for two-level A the rank-dependent sum of paired square-root eigenvalue gaps is an explicit sharp answer for the whole unitary orbit, with every intermediate trace attained. This is a natural constrained-invariant classification with an exact optimizer and a clear use for spectral stability analysis, not merely a finite table, renaming, or a tiny numerical improvement.
